title: Adaptive probe sampler and throttle strategy for cross-region autoscaler resilience
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Background: We observed two incidents where aggressive readiness probe fanout + global autoscaler reactions caused cascading regional tape-outs and prolonged degraded latency for multi-region customers. The root cause analysis shows mismatched sampling windows between probe emission, synthetic warmups, and autoscaler evaluation leading to thrash during regional failover and a spike in circuit-breaker activations.

Goal: Implement an adaptive probe sampling and short-term throttle controller that smooths readiness signal injection for the central autoscaler, reducing false-positive scale downs and preventing unnecessary cross-region failovers while preserving fast detection of true degradations. This should improve SLO adherence (p95 latency and availability) for cross-region traffic and reduce load-shedding events during transient infra disturbances.

Scope:
- Implement a probe sampler at the region edge that adjusts probe frequency per instance based on a confidence score (recent success ratio, request latency drift, kv-cache hit rate).
- Introduce a transient-throttle window in the autoscaler ingestion path that temporarily weights down probe failures when there is correlated network noise or global rollout activity.
- Add a small circuit-breaker gating layer that can route affected traffic to warm fallback model variant (lower-cost compute path) when regional health transitions are ambiguous.
- Ensure all changes are observable: new metrics for probe-sample-rate, probe-confidence, throttle-factor, and circuit-breaker activations; dashboards and alerts for regression detection.

Acceptance criteria:
- End-to-end test demonstrating reduced autoscaler thrash in a synthetic regional packet-loss scenario: 60% reduction in scale-up/scale-down cycles over 10 minutes vs baseline.
- No regression on mean time-to-detect real degradations (target: within 30s of sustained error spike).
- Dashboards capturing new signals are live and connected to incident runbooks.
- Feature rollouts gated by canary in one region and gradual ramp (0%, 10%, 50%, 100%) with automatic rollback on increased SLO error rate.

Design notes & trade-offs:
- We prefer probabilistic sampling to reduce probe fanout cost; downside is slightly slower detection for single-instance hard failures. Mitigation: keep liveness checks unchanged for definitive hard-failure detection.
- Throttle windows introduce inertia to autoscaler decisions which reduces responsiveness to real faults; countermeasure is confidence scoring which bypasses throttle for high-severity signals (e.g., consecutive 5xxs + latency > 2x baseline).
- Circuit-breaker fallback uses a compatible model variant with lower resource footprint. There is a small cost to accuracy; rollout will include quality monitoring to ensure acceptable regressions.

Implementation plan:
1) Prototype sampler + confidence heuristic in staging traffic router (2 weeks).
2) Autoscaler ingestion change to accept throttle-factor metadata and backpressure-aware scoring (1 week).
3) Circuit-breaker fallback plumbing + model routing config (1 week).
4) Observability: metrics, dashboards, and runbook updates (1 week).
5) Canary rollout and ramp (2 weeks).

Monitoring & SLOs:
- New SLO targets for region availability: maintain >= 99.9% per-region availability during failover window.
- Track probe false-positive rate, autoscaler cycle rate, circuit-breaker activations per 10k requests.
- Alerting: if autoscaler cycle rate increases 2x above baseline or p95 latency regresses >15% during rollout, pause ramp and auto-roll back.

QA and testing:
- Chaos tests with packet loss, increased latency, and KV cache degradation in 'blue' region while traffic shifts to 'green'.
- Integration test harness reproducing previous incidents with baseline vs new approach.
- Load test to verify probe sampler scales with fleet size.

Rollout & migration:
- Feature flag gated per-region. Start with non-critical EU region, monitor 72h, then roll to US-west, then to global.
- Backfill historical probe samples into metrics aggregator for correlation analysis (one-off migration script).

comments: 2026-02-19 - Asha Patel: Created ticket after incident postmortem. Initial design sketched in RFC link above. Requested Diego for engineering estimate.

2026-02-22 - Diego Morales: Spun up a small prototype that samples readiness checks at 10% and repro'ed autoscaler stabilization in local sim. Early results look promising; sample confidence heuristic needs tuning for latency-sensitive routes.

2026-02-26 - Lin Chen (SRE): Review: prefer retention of liveness check path to ensure node eviction still happens on hard failures. Also requested per-customer opt-out for aggressive sampling to avoid affecting enterprise tenants in compliance mode.
2026-03-02 - Riley Nguyen (PM): Approved P1 prioritization. Asked for explicit rollback criteria and should link to console rollout controls so ops can disable per-region during incidents.
2026-03-06 - Diego Morales: Implemented throttle-factor ingestion and added metric probe_throttle_factor. Pushed prototype PR 3142 for review. Unit tests added for sampler behavior under jitter.

2026-03-09 - Security review (A. Kaur): Quick assessment - no key material exposure, but requested additional logging audit for circuit-breaker decisions. Marked security_review_required=false but audit logging required.

2026-03-12 - Diego Morales: Canary started in eu-west-2 at 10%. First 24h: autoscaler cycle rate down 48% vs baseline, p95 latency unchanged. Will proceed to 50% tomorrow. Linking canary dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/canary/probe-sampler-eu-west-2
next_steps: Finish sampler confidence tuning by 2026-03-18. Complete canary ramp to 50% then 100% with 72h observation windows. Prepare rollback playbook and console toggle for ops.
notes: Avoid coupling sampler rate to billing tiers for now; keep it solely behavioral. We should evaluate cost savings after full rollout and consider exposing an opt-in autoscaler aggressiveness knob for enterprise customers later.
